pull.title: wallet: Only broadcast resubmitted transactions that were added to the mempool
pull.body:
As discussed in #36403, one of the issues with current rebroadcast behavior is that the rebroadcast begins an unconditional relay of a transaction to peers. While this is broadcast is limited to peers that have not previously been inv'd the transaction, there is still a privacy leak in this double relay of a transaction, especially so for transactions that are still in nodes' mempools.

This PR changes the rebroadcast to only rebroadcast transactions if the transaction was not already present in our mempool. This provides some additional privacy while retaining intended rebroadcast behavior as transactions that have likely fallen out of nodes' mempools are the ones that actually need to be rebroadcast.

The wallet rebroadcast tests are additionally refactored for isolation so that their behaviors can still be tested after this change. Additionally, a test for the loading resubmission was added, as well as a test for the new behavior.

events.message: test: Refactor wallet_resendwallettransactions for test case isolation
test: Test wallet unconfirmed resubmission on load

node: Add option to relay txs only if they are added to mempool

BroadcastTransaction takes different modes of broadcasting. Add one
which will attempt to add a transaction to the mempool, and if that
succeeds, broadcast the transaction to peers. If the transaction already
exists in the mempool, it will not be rebroadcast.
wallet: Only rebroadcast transactions that were re-added to the mempool
test: Check that wallet txs already in the mempool are not rebroadcast

Ideally, start with the one that should be merged first.

This PR introduces the new `MEMPOOL_AND_BROADCAST_ADDED` TxBroadcast case, and uses it when the wallet resubmits transactions to the node’s mempool instead of the transaction being rebroadcast to all peers that it hadn’t been inventoried. The tests check that the rebroadcast happens when the transaction is added to the mempool and doesn’t happen when the transaction was already present. This is an obvious privacy improvement.

The only open question I have at the moment is whether the combination of using `MEMPOOL_NO_BROADCAST` on wallet loading and then `MEMPOOL_AND_BROADCAST_ADDED` on the wallet’s rebroadcast could prevent a transaction from being resubmitted to the network. E.g., if a wallet submits a low-feerate transaction, then the node is turned off for some period during which a feerate spike causes most of the network to drop the transaction, then the node is turned back on, wouldn’t this mean that the wallet’s transaction is not rebroadcast at all?

Also, I’m not sure whether using `MEMPOOL_AND_BROADCAST_ADDED` during wallet loading would fix that, if the node still had the transaction in its mempool from before going offline.

After a restart, this branch does not announce a wallet transaction that peers already received while our own mempool keeps it, so the answer to murch's question is yes.

I built 4dbd27f37b and its base f739c7876b and ran a regtest script that connects a fresh P2PInterface peer, moves mocktime 36 hours ahead so that MaybeResendWalletTxs runs, and sends an unrelated transaction as a barrier. A wallet transaction still in the mempool is announced on base and not on the branch, as intended. One that expired and was accepted again is announced on both. One rejected as non-final is announced on neither.

With -persistmempool=0, the load-time resubmission puts the transaction back without broadcast. With mempool.dat, it comes back already out of the unbroadcast set, because a peer requested it before shutdown. The branch announced nothing in either case, and with -persistmempool=0 nothing over two periodic resubmissions and six ReattemptInitialBroadcast windows; base announced it at each resubmission. The same holds whenever our mempool keeps a transaction that peers dropped, until it expires from our mempool (two weeks by default). A node offline for days now takes its own mempool as a proxy for everyone else's. test_resubmit_on_load stops before the first periodic resubmission; extending it would pin whichever behaviour is intended.

Smaller: the comment above ResubmitWalletTransactions still names MEMPOOL_AND_BROADCAST_TO_ALL for the periodic path, and "resubmit N unconfirmed transactions" now counts transactions not relayed. I can share the script as a gist.

ACK 4dbd27f37b52e49a8d392bd2ee6713ae7dcf23df modulo https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36482#discussion_r4567017959

As for the @murchandamus scenario:

* a transaction is submitted, ends up in the mempool and in the network
* the node is shut down
* fee pressure causes the network to forget about the transaction
* the fee pressure eases on the network
* the node is started
  * at wallet load it will not broadcast the transaction
  * 12-36h later it will not broadcast either because the transaction is in its mempool

https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36481 would help in that case to manually rebroadcast the transaction.

Concept ACK.
Worth noting that a node with a small mempool can still resubmit and rebroadcast a tx while others have it and won't relay it, so it still has the same leak even with this change. Adding a separate option to disable rebroadcast, ideally off by default, would be useful. That way, it's opt-in for advanced users who need it.

Post-Coredev, I discussed the issue with a few others in BRW, and made a post about what I understand thus far. https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/exploiting-wallet-rebroadcast-to-link-addresses-to-node-ips-and-more/3123

This assumes that the transaction to be evicted, the one that spends `conflict_utxo`, has a fee rate less than `30`. That is a bit obscure and fragile.

Consider getting the feerate of the transaction to be evicted and using a higher value than that (plus two more asserts - that the to-be-evicted transaction is in the mempool when the function starts and is absent at the end):

The newly added `wait_for_single_broadcast()` is almost identical to the existent `wait_for_broadcast()`. I wonder if the existent function can be modified to use `>=` instead of `==` when comparing the sets. This would allow the input list of txids to be a subset of the `tx_invs_received`.

Or if that is going to break something then take a parameter to control whether to use `==` or `>=`.
